My name is Morgan Voltz. A full-stack developer, I am preparing the Licence professionnelle Métiers de l'informatique (a professional Bachelor's degree, EQF level 6) at the Université de Haute-Alsace (UHA 4.0 programme, in three university diplomas) and, alongside that, I run Kovelt, the company I founded. I am looking for a six-month internship from January 2027, with the aim of continuing in a work-study programme for the rest of the course and for the Master's I am aiming for next. This page sums up my background; every project named links to its full write-up in the portfolio.

## Education

- **Licence professionnelle Métiers de l'informatique (software design, development and testing), UHA 4.0 programme** — Université de Haute-Alsace, Mulhouse, 2025–2028. The programme is made of three university diplomas: DU 4.0.1, DU 4.0.2 (in progress, for the second time: a first session in 2025–2026 had GeoForge, the game, as its storyline project (the « fil rouge » of the programme); current storyline project: MomoCad, since September 2026) and DU 4.0.3, on completion of which the Licence is awarded, expected in 2028. First-year storyline project (4.0.1): UHA Learn. First-year client project: AUTOFIN Control, for m2A (Mulhouse Alsace Agglomération), in a team of five.
- **Work-study Master's in Computer Science and Mobility** — Université de Haute-Alsace, Mulhouse, planned for 2028–2030.
- **BTS (two-year higher technical diploma) in Electronic Systems** (first year) — embedded programming in C/C++, robotics in Python.
- **Vocational baccalaureate in digital electronic systems (Bac pro SEN)**, networks and fire safety option — Siemens systems, alarm control panels.

## Professional experience

- **Founder and developer — Kovelt** (since September 2025). I design, build and operate three products on my own: [carbon-fr](../projects/carbon-fr-en.md), a Rust API in production; [Atlas](../projects/atlas-en.md), in C# / .NET 10; and [Vefta](../projects/vefta-en.md), a personal productivity suite in Rust (Axum, Dioxus, PostgreSQL), offline-first and never monetising the user's data.
- **Industrial electrician, then automation technician** (before the career change). Some fifteen years as an electrician: access control, alarm and fire detection panels; industrial and commercial electrical work; site supervision. Then automation technician, including programming Siemens PLCs on stacker cranes, the logistics robots of Stöcklin Logistik AG (Switzerland).

## Technical skills

### Languages
Rust, C#, TypeScript / JavaScript, PHP, Python, SQL, C/C++ — and, more occasionally, Lua and Pascal.

### Frameworks and libraries
Axum, ASP.NET Core, Entity Framework Core, REST APIs, React, Dioxus, Twig, HTML/CSS, Three.js; PostgreSQL and MySQL as database engines.

### Architecture and methods
Clean Architecture, hexagonal architecture, microservices, Agile, MCP/ACP (integration protocols for AI agents); agentic development framed by ADRs (architecture decision records) that settle the architecture, the stack and the security before the code.

### Tools
Git, Docker / Podman, GitLab CI/CD, Postman / Bruno, Linux, WSL2, Jira, Confluence, Slack; personal self-hosting (GitLab, Nextcloud, Penpot).

## Languages

- **French** — native language.
- **German** — fluent, B2 level: daily professional use for twelve years in German-speaking Switzerland.
- **Swiss German** — spoken and understood.
- **English** — B2 level, technical and professional: I document some projects bilingually, GeoForge, the Godot addon, for instance.

## Selected projects

### Products and client projects
- **[Vefta](../projects/vefta-en.md)** — end-to-end Rust productivity suite for Kovelt, offline-first. *In progress.*
- **[Atlas](../projects/atlas-en.md)** — .NET platform that unifies French public company and industrial property data, locked down by tests. *In progress.*
- **[carbon-fr](../projects/carbon-fr-en.md)** — open source API that measures the carbon intensity of French electricity. *Stable.*
- **[AUTOFIN Control](../projects/autofin-control-en.md)** — reading PDF balance sheets by geometric analysis for the financial control of m2A, in a team of five. *Stable.*

### Storyline and academic projects, UHA 4.0
- **[MomoCad](../projects/momocad-en.md)** — CAD-style 2D drawing whose state is nothing but a replayed event log; current 4.0.2 storyline project. *In progress.*
- **[GeoForge, the game](../projects/geoforge-jeu-en.md)** — geometric puzzle where only the server validates a placement; 4.0.2 storyline project of the 2025–2026 session, led and defended solo. *Archived.*
- **[UHA Learn](../projects/uha-learn-en.md)** — course catalogue and progress tracking, with a PHP REST API written without a framework; 4.0.1 storyline project. *Archived.*
- **[HEHEWATT](../projects/hehewatt-en.md)** — school carpooling application taken over and extended by several cohorts of students, in a team of 30 to 50 people depending on the cohort. *Archived.*

### Tooling and personal prototypes
- **[DevEye](../projects/deveye-en.md)** — MCP server in Rust that gives an AI agent eyes and hands on a live graphical application. *In progress.*
- **[GeoForge, the Godot addon](../projects/geoforge-godot-en.md)** — generation of relief, rivers and roads from real physical laws, adjustable point by point. *Prototype.*
- **[chronos-penpot-tools](../projects/chronos-penpot-tools-en.md)** — Penpot plugin that turns a mock-up into a Dioxus component, through a conversion core compiled to WebAssembly. *Prototype.*
- **[Trace 4.0, Manifest V3 migration](../projects/trace-4-0-manifest-v3-en.md)** — getting the school's activity-tracking extension, broken by the end of Manifest V2, working again on my own initiative. *Stable.*
- **[xvii](../projects/xvii-en.md)** — sixteen-track audio studio in Rust whose real-time thread may neither allocate nor wait. *Prototype.*
- **[ancestors-modding](../projects/ancestors-modding-en.md)** — reverse-engineering toolbox to mod an abandoned Unreal Engine game with no SDK and no documentation. *Prototype.*

## Interests

Musician (singer in Breath from the void, a metal band), 3D printing and technical drawing, digital sovereignty and free software, game development (Bevy/Rust), embedded electronics.

My name is Morgan Voltz. Before I wrote my first real line of code, I spent some fifteen years in hands-on work, and that detour shapes the way I work today.

## A path that did not start with software

I studied electronics for five years: my first programs were C for microcontrollers, and my first logic gates date from then. I then spent about fifteen years in the field, mostly in German-speaking Switzerland, working in German every day, as an electrician on access control, security and fire detection systems, up to supervising construction sites. I later became an automation technician. I taught myself programming again, out of frustration at not finding tools that fitted what I needed. When the opportunity came, I chose to go back to university to become a full-stack developer: a personal choice, not one steered by school, and I present it as a strength rather than a detour to justify.

## What I like to build

Learning a new language or a new framework does not scare me: that is the whole point of being full-stack. Day to day I use C#, Rust, PHP, Python, JavaScript or TypeScript, with React, xUnit or Dioxus depending on the project. A bug or a problem I cannot solve yet is a challenge before it is an obstacle. Alongside the projects of my training I run Kovelt, my company, where I build Vefta, a productivity suite written in Rust; I also contribute to open source tools.

## How I work

I am used to Clean Architecture and hexagonal architecture, and I take a close interest in microservices. Before I start working with an AI agent (Claude Code first, though I can adapt to others), I write ADRs (architecture decision records) that settle the project's architecture, stack and security, so that the agent never drifts from the brief: a strict method that lets me move fast without losing quality. I also rely on these agents for security audits, for hunting down monoliths and, in lower-level languages, for catching memory corruption. I test systematically, the architecture itself included, so that an automated check enforces the rules rather than a mere honour system. I work in an agile way, in class as in personal projects, with Jira, GitLab, Slack and the other Atlassian tools; I host my own GitLab, Nextcloud and Penpot on a personal VPS. I also keep learning every week by following technology developments, with ongoing subscriptions to Udemy and OpenClassrooms.

## What I am looking for

I am preparing the Licence professionnelle Métiers de l'informatique (professional Bachelor's degree, EQF level 6) at UHA, on the UHA 4.0 programme, which comprises three DU (university diploma) stages, 4.0.1 to 4.0.3. I am currently in DU 4.0.2, and the Licence is awarded on completion of DU 4.0.3, in 2028. I then aim for the work-study Master's in Computer Science and Mobility: artificial intelligence and software architecture interest me equally. I am looking for a six-month internship from January 2027, then a work-study programme for the rest of the course, a rhythm that leaves time for classes and for my own projects.

## Away from the code

I do 3D printing and technical drawing, and I sing in a metal band, Breath from the void.
